svg.title: CopperDragon Sparrow framework kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: three China-nexus clusters sharing the Sparrow toolset tracked by Check Point as CopperDragon; SilentDelivery watering holes with a fake Chrome certificate warning and a Certificate Fix MSI that delivers SquadC, plus an ftp.exe LNK phishing variant; OceanGate intrusion of internet-facing Linux servers with AnnobinDoor and SparrowShell and RDP brute force to Windows; CopperAdu hidden admin and WinDivert passive backdoor; DarkWire DLL sideloading, CopperDNS and LSASS dumping against Latin American telecoms; detection anchors are the C2 paths, the admin$ account, sideloading pairs and comsvcs LSASS dumps.
svg.text: CopperDragon: the Sparrow framework across SilentDelivery, OceanGate and DarkWire
Vendor: Check Point Research (2026-11-10) · Date: 2026-11-16 · Cluster: CopperDragon (medium) · Day 146
CHINA-NEXUS ESPIONAGE LANE
Cluster map: CopperDragon, a possible quartermaster for China-nexus actors [T1583 T1587.001]
Check Point (2026-11-10) links SilentDelivery, OceanGate and DarkWire through the shared Sparrow framework (Windows and Linux)
Actors using the toolset: FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, Tropic Trooper, UAT-9244; Salt Typhoon relationship stays unclear
Targets: telecom, government, military, research and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia and Europe
SparrowDoor SparrowShell SquadC CopperDoor
SilentDelivery: watering hole with a fake Chrome SSL error and a Certificate Fix MSI [T1189 T1204.002]
jsjiami-obfuscated JS on compromised sites polls /image-check?t=, posts the page URL to /report-url, then shows Install certificate
CertFixer.msi from compromised S3 buckets delivers SquadC (runs only if a browser is present) or a SparrowDoor variant
Phishing variant: RAR with a .docx.lnk that abuses ftp.exe to run a batch file named info.dll (Indonesia)
/image-check?t= /report-url /register-ip CertFixer.msi
OceanGate: internet-facing Linux first, then Windows through RDP brute force [T1190 T1110 T1021.001]
AnnobinDoor (Go) and SparrowShell (modular, modified Reptile rootkit) plus trojanized ssh and sshd for credential logging
FRPC, Chisel and a port scanner for tunnelling; repeated RDP logons with different passwords until an admin account works
Same TLS certificate SHA-1 as SilentDelivery C2 links the two clusters
annobinagent /tmp/%x xmain 0x11223344
Windows post-exploitation: CopperAdu hidden admin, keylogger, LSA credential theft [T1136.001 T1056.001 T1003]
net user admin$ ... /add, LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=1, firewall rule RasiUwpApp opens TCP 445
CopperLogger Raw Input keylogger (window kbl), CopperLsa custom SSP in LSASS, CopperList inventory with LZNT1
SparrowDoor variant embeds WinDivert: passive backdoor behind a legitimate port such as 443 (internal listener e.g. 49628)
admin$ RasiUwpApp WinDivert kbl
DarkWire: sideloading, CopperDNS and LSASS dumping in Latin America [T1574.002 T1071.004 T1003.001]
Sideloading pairs such as libvlccore.dll with vlc.exe and winfsp.dll with fsptool.exe, staged in existing system or vendor folders
CopperDNS tunnels over DNS MX queries; CopperProxy SOCKS5 (rule ss1); SoftEther renamed vmtoolsd.exe or csrss.exe; SMB and wmiexec
LSASS dump through comsvcs.dll, output renamed 1.png; shared domain amelicen[.]com
comsvcs.dll 1.png amelicen[.]com port 6532
Response and break points [no technique]
Block the listed domains and IPs at DNS and proxy only after re-validation; alert on the three JS C2 paths and the shared certificate
Hunt admin$ accounts, sideloaded DLLs outside install paths, comsvcs MiniDump and WindowsUpdateAssist values; patch exposed Linux services
About 40 percent of the Check Point page was read via a summary: confirm hashes against the primary IOC section
ftp.exe LNK | admin$ | sideload | comsvcs
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-05 (+03b), KQL k1-k3, YARA (3 rules), Suricata sids 9995001-9995006, PEAK H1-H3. Heuristic; not compiled or run on telemetry.
Break points: JS C2 paths, admin$ account, sideloading outside install paths, comsvcs LSASS dump. Indicators decay: re-validate.
